statement.essentials: A pleomorphic adenoma’s outer layer is often thin or incomplete, and small finger-like extensions can reach beyond it, which is why surgeons take a cuff of normal gland rather than shelling the tumour out.
statement.anatomy: Most pleomorphic adenomas have at least one capsular feature: an incomplete capsule, penetration of the capsule, pseudopodia or satellite nodules. Left in the surrounding gland, pseudopodia and satellite tumours can cause recurrence.
statement.clinical: Of 218 resected parotid pleomorphic adenomas, 73% had at least one capsular feature: incomplete capsule in 33%, capsular penetration in 26%, pseudopodia in 40% and satellite nodules in 13%. Incomplete capsule and satellites were commonest in the stroma-rich (myxoid) subtype.

limitations: One centre’s series of resected tumours; the authors report these features are more common than earlier literature suggested, and that the prospective group had more pseudopodia and capsular penetration. The inset drawing is a schematic of these features, not a section of a real tumour.
